sections.text:
1 Hunc libellum ab Isaac monacho minimum sexagenario m. octobri a. 1372
scriptum edidit D. Petavius in Uranologio, p. 359 sqq. (de temporibus cf. p. 362,
364b, 381d) , [= De Doctrina temporum, Antverpiae, 1703, t. III, p. 195 sqq.] Cf.
Usener, op. cit., p. 5, n. 1.
2 De Hephaestionis excerptis, cf. cod. 8, f. 33 sqq. et Studi ital. di Filologia
classica, t. VI, p. 2 sqq., ubi ostendimus codices Parisinos, quibus Engelbrecht usus
est, ex Laurentianis supplendos esse.
sections.en:
1 This little book written by the monk Isaac, at least sixty years old, in the month of October in the year 1372
was edited by D. Petavius in Uranologion, p. 359 sqq. (concerning the times cf. p. 362,
364b, 381d) , [= De Doctrina temporum, Antwerp, 1703, vol. III, p. 195 sqq.] Cf.
Usener, op. cit., p. 5, n. 1.
2 Concerning the excerpts of Hephaestion, cf. cod. 8, f. 33 sqq. and Studi ital. di Filologia
classica, vol. VI, p. 2 sqq., where we have shown that the Parisian codices, which Engelbrecht used,
must be supplemented from the Laurentian ones.

summary.headline: Florentine Astrological Manuscript Catalog
summary.text: Catalog entries for a Florentine astrological manuscript covering planetary longitude and latitude, synodic and eclipse calculations, zodiacal transitions, palmistry prognostics, canons, city-coordinate tables, and works by Isaac Argyros and Hephaestion of Thebes. The apparatus cites D. Petavius, Usener, and Engelbrecht and notes material from Laurentian and Parisian codices.
